title: Epochal traffic tilt with stream habit restoration
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Hosted API gateway must support active-active cross-region failover while preserving streaming sessions and minimizing client-visible disruptions. Recent incidents showed token replays and stream resets during abrupt regional cutovers. This ticket defines an epochal tilt strategy: a controlled, telemetry-gated gradual traffic shift (tilt) that preserves stream continuity where possible and degrades gracefully when not.
description_long:
Goals:
- Maintain API SLOs: 99.95% availability for request/response paths and 99.5% continuity for streaming sessions (no unexpected disconnects or >1s replay gaps for active streams).
- Provide predictable failover behavior: bounded user-visible reconnection window and clear fallback when continuity is not possible.
- Keep per-token and per-request cost impact modest (target <15% extra infra during tilt).

High-level approach:
1) Epoch model: define discrete epochs (30s-2m windows) during which a fraction of new requests are routed to the target region. Increase weight in steps: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% if telemetry stays healthy. Each epoch boundary produces a short handshake window to allow stream resumes.
2) Session affinity: recognize active streaming sessions by durable session-id and resume-token. For sessions with resume-token, attempt transparent continuation via token-stitching (server-to-server checkpoint exchange across regions). If resume-token absent or incompatible, prefer sticky routing to original region until TTL expires.
3) KV cache sync: lightweight checkpoint of KV cache metadata during tilt epochs. Avoid full KV transfer; rely on prefix/KV cache warm-up and short-term fallbacks to bloom-filter based cold-path.
4) Circuit breakers: multi-dimensional CBs triggered by (a) error-rate >5% sustained over 1m, (b) sudden p99 latency regression >200ms relative to baseline, (c) queue depth >75% of capacity. Breaker action: freeze further epoch increases, roll back to previous epoch, and open short-lived denial for non-critical classes.
5) Load-shedding: SLO-aware tiered shedding. First shed non-SLAd background requests (analytics, large-context offline embeddings), then degrade long-context requests (truncate context heuristics), then if still overloaded apply global token-rate caps and reject new sessions for lowest-tier customers.

Decision trade-offs:
- Immediate cutover vs epochal tilt: Immediate cutover has low implementation complexity but caused larger streaming disruptions in past incidents. Epochal tilt increases complexity (resume-token exchange, KV sync) but preserves user sessions and gives observability windows.
- Synchronous KV replication vs checkpointing: Chosen checkpoint + warm-up reduces cross-region bandwidth and avoids stalls, at cost of temporary cold-path misses.
- Transparent token stitching vs client reconnect: We implement token stitching for short-lived sessions (<10m) and allow client reconnect fallback for long idle sessions to reduce complexity and storage of long-lived KV snapshots.

Rolling plan and runbook (summary):
- Preflight (automated): ensure target region capacity, warm model weights, run synthetic streaming smoke tests (10k simulated concurrent streams).
- Canary epoch (5% weight, 5m): monitor errors, p99 latency, stream-resume success rate.
- Progressive epochs: increase weights with 10m observation windows; rollback on CB triggers.
- Finalization: shift DNS/egress weight and drain old region gracefully (30m drain).
- Postmortem: collect traces, token-stitch logs, and KV warm-up stats.

SLOs & Alerts:
- Availability SLO: 99.95% for single-request flows (monitor via synthetic checks and production p99 success).
- Streaming continuity SLO: 99.5% measured as fraction of active sessions that complete without server-initiated reset or >1s token gap during tilt windows.
- Alert thresholds: streaming-continuity-drop >1% within 10m -> Pager; p99 latency regression >150ms sustained 3m -> Pager; error-rate >3% sustained 2m -> Pager; CB open event -> Ops channel.

Circuit breaker parameters (initial):
- Error-rate CB: open if >=5% errors over sliding 60s window; half-open after 30s; exponential backoff on repeated opens.
- Latency CB: open if p99 increases by >200ms relative to baseline for 60s.
- Resource CB: open if GPU memory pressure >85% or queue depth >75% for 90s.

Streaming specifics:
- Resume token protocol: opaque resume-token carrying last-ack sequence id + minimal KV sketch. Tokens are short-lived (TTL 10m).
- Stitching handshake: source region exports minimal checkpoint to secure S3 (encrypted) or direct control-plane tunnel for target region to import. For private deployments, use VPC peering path.
- Fallback: if stitching fails, client is asked to reconnect and resume using client-side exponential backoff with jitter. Provide transparent 503 with Resume-After header and auto-backoff guidance in SDKs.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- New Grafana dashboard: tilt-epochs, per-epoch success/failure, stream-resume-rate, KV-warmup-hitrate, circuit-breaker events.
- Tracing: distributed traces propagate resume-token id to link events across regions.
- Cost metrics: additional instance-hours, cross-region egress, and cold-path token penalty tracked per-epoch.

Testing & validation:
- Integration test harness: simulating active-active tilt under synthetic load (variable context lengths, adversarial reconnects).
- Chaos test: randomly drop checkpoint transfers and force CB opens to validate rollback behavior.
- Canary: 3 customers in target canary group streaming real traffic.

Open questions / risks:
- Long-lived sessions (>1h) semantics and storage of long resume tokens (risk: state explosion). Proposed mitigation: require explicit session heartbeat to extend token TTL, or migrate long sessions to dedicated capacity.
- Cross-region regulatory constraints (data residency): ensure KV checkpointing path is only used if permitted; otherwise force client reconnect fallback.
- Client SDK adoption: resume-token handshake requires SDK changes; fallbacks must not break older SDKs.

Artifacts & links:
- Runbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/epochal-tilt-runbook
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/drive/epochal-tilt-design-v1.pdf
- Draft PR (server): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4121
- Grafana tilt dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tilt/active-tilt-overview

Success criteria (post-rollout):
- No pager from streaming continuity during full roll to 100%.
- Measured streaming continuity >=99.5% during tilt windows for 72h of production traffic.
- Cost delta <=15% sustained during roll and amortized back to baseline within 48h of finalization.

Next steps:
- Finalize resume-token format and SDK contract (owner: SDK team).
- Implement checkpoint exporter and secure short-lived transfer tokens (owner: infra).
- Wire telemetry and create canary gating automation (owner: SRE).
comments: 2026-03-02 Maya Chen: Initial draft complete. Shared with SRE and SDK leads for feedback. Added preliminary CB thresholds based on last incident baselines.

2026-03-04 Omar Ruiz: Design review notes: prefer ephemeral control-plane tunnel over S3 for resume-token exchange in hosted environments. Asked infra to prototype. Added latency CB tightening to 150ms alerting for early detection.

2026-03-06 Priya Singh (SRE): Performed stress test v1. Observed stream-resume success 92% at 20% tilt with KV warm-up disabled. With lightweight KV warm-up active success rose to 98%. Recommended increasing epoch windows to 10m for warm-up under high concurrency.

2026-03-08 Design review (Sofia Novak): Recommended SDK compatibility header to negotiate resume-token support; otherwise servers should not attempt stitching for older clients. Added note to PR template.
2026-03-10 Omar Ruiz: Implemented CB instrumentation and initial Grafana panels. Draft PR created: runtime#4121. Scheduling canary for 2026-03-15 (internal customers).
